chunks: It is as though I see him advancing with an army which has neither dust nor noise, nor rustling of reins, nor neighing of horses. They are trampling the ground with their feet as if they are the feet of ostriches.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the silent army described in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) describes a silent, swift army whose lack of dust and noise signifies a stealthy, overwhelming advance, a prophecy widely interpreted by Shia scholars as referring to the Mongol conquests or the Khwarazmian forces. The comparison to ostrich feet highlights their unique mobility and the suddenness of their arrival, serving as a sign of divine judgment upon the Umayyad and Abbasid eras for their deviation from justice.

en.sayed-ali-raza: It is as though I see him advancing with an army which has neither dust nor noise, nor rustling of reins, nor neighing of horses. They are trampling the ground with their feet as if they are the feet of ostriches.
